facts.heading: Anxiety worsened in September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and this feeling got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September.

facts.heading: Promotion at school
facts.content: Hannah has taught at her school for 11 years. She was asked to step up when the deputy left.
facts.evidence: I've taught here for 11 years and I have loved it and then they had asked me to step up when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being inadequate
facts.content: Hannah worries that people will notice she does not know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety symptoms on Sunday evenings
facts.content: On Sunday evenings, Hannah's chest feels tight, and she rehearses the next day's staff meeting in her head.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings, my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Fear of being perceived as incompetent
facts.content: Hannah fears people will think she is out of her depth or that she is a teacher who cannot read.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice earful teacher who can't actually read.

facts.heading: Rewriting email to governors
facts.content: Last week, Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of Mr. Hargraves's opinion
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think she was stupid regarding the behavior policy change.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Feeling of inauthenticity
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about being capable, as if she is pretending.
facts.evidence: About being capable, as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Comparison to mother's career
facts.content: Hannah compares her current role to her mother's, who was a headteacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother's support and advice
facts.content: Hannah's mother is supportive on the surface and says Hannah worries too much.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Waking up at 4 AM
facts.content: Hannah wakes up at 4 AM every morning and goes through her to-do list.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at 4 every morning. I fall asleep fine.

facts.heading: Caffeine intake for energy
facts.content: Hannah drinks five or six cups of coffee to get through the day.
facts.evidence: Five or six, then I can't sit still in the afternoons.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms in afternoons
facts.content: In the afternoons, Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Last Thursday, Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday, I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water.

facts.heading: Partner Ben's advice
facts.content: Hannah's partner, Ben, suggests she should just enjoy the promotion.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it.

facts.heading: Feeling guilty about partner's advice
facts.content: Hannah feels guilty and alone when Ben tells her to enjoy the promotion.
facts.evidence: Guilty and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Loss of school friendships
facts.content: Hannah no longer eats lunch with her former classmates because she is now their line manager.
facts.evidence: Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward.

facts.heading: Missing teaching experience
facts.content: Hannah misses the children and the daily experience of a child learning something new.
facts.evidence: The children mostly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time.

facts.heading: Regret accepting promotion
facts.content: Hannah cried after accepting the promotion because she felt she couldn't say no to her superior.
facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried.

facts.heading: Felt relaxed during summer holidays
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays.
facts.evidence: These summer holidays. We went walking in the lakes and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Supportive people say well done
facts.content: Hannah feels that people around her only say 'well done' instead of asking her about her feelings.
facts.evidence: Nobody has asked me that, they just say well done.

facts.heading: Wreck before term started
facts.content: Hannah felt like a wreck the week before the term started.
facts.evidence: The week before term, I was a wreck again.

facts.heading: Could not eat on Sunday
facts.content: Hannah could not eat on the Sunday before the term started.
facts.evidence: I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down positives
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening, including small things.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening.

facts.heading: Stopped writing down positives
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing in her notebook after about two weeks because she felt silly.
facts.evidence: It held for about two weeks, and then I stopped because I felt silly.

facts.heading: Desire to do job without feeling fraud
facts.content: Hannah would like to do her job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: would like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.heading: Goal: No rehearsal in meetings
facts.content: Hannah's goal is to walk into a meeting without rehearsing beforehand.
facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing at first.

facts.heading: Goal: No stomach knots on Sunday
facts.content: Hannah's goal is to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without her stomach being in knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Shared feeling of being lighter
facts.content: Hannah felt lighter after stating her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lighter. A bit tearful actually.

facts.heading: Disclosed severe symptoms to therapist
facts.content: Hannah stated that this is the first time she has told anyone how bad things are.
facts.evidence: It's the first time I have told anyone how bad it is.

facts.heading: Kept 4am issue from Ben
facts.content: Hannah has not told Ben about her 4am issue.
facts.evidence: Not even Ben knows how about the 4am.

facts.heading: Plans to tell Ben this week
facts.content: Hannah might try telling Ben about the issue this week.
facts.evidence: I might try this week.

facts.heading: Preferred time to talk to Ben
facts.content: Hannah prefers to talk to Ben on Saturday morning over breakfast.
facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps?

facts.heading: Agreed to try evening notebook again
facts.content: Hannah agreed to try the evening notebook again, even if only for one line.
facts.evidence: I could. I will put it by the kettle so I don't forget.

facts.heading: Glad she attended session
facts.content: Hannah was glad she did not cancel the session that morning.
facts.evidence: lady I nearly cancelled this morning. I'm glad I didn't.
